██, ██, N.F.113
MBCC Headquarters,
Chief's Office

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: So, you believe that Nirvana, or perhaps someone behind them, was the driving force behind the two Rustfire crises in N.F. 104 and N.F. 113, correct?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: What a dangerous speculation. But it's not surprising that you would think that way.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: After all, you yourself got entangled in it. Even death could be exploited…

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: It's not that complicated. All I want is the truth.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: The truth, huh…

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: How many of those who chase the truth at all costs can actually afford its price?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: And what do you plan to do once you find it? Make the big shot who pulled the trigger on you pay in blood?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: Easy, it's just a joke.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: Regardless, the puppet master won't be an easy opponent...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: Please pay close attention to your new guest.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I will...

You know who the man is warning you about. That S-Class Sinner from the FAC who turned up following an abrupt staff transfer. In fact, you've been on your guard since the day Rahu arrived at the MBCC.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: It seems you've already figured it out.
The official from the 9th Agency takes out a well-sealed document from his briefcase and places it on the office desk with a smile.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: This is what you're looking for... The 9th Agency won't prevent you from probing for the so-called truth. But remember…

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Member
steps.content: Stay safe.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: State your purpose.
Under the bright light, the woman's face is shrouded in shadow.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: You call this a routine interrogation?
Rahu looks around. The cramped interrogation room is filled only with the hum of cold surveillance equipment and halogen lamps.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You've accepted your transfer to the MBCC and you're an S-Class Sinner. Undergoing this form of investigation is your duty.
Rahu looks into your eyes, and after a moment, a cold, emotionless smile appears on her face.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Yes, <color=#fb9259><size=40>Commander</size></color>.
You take out a document envelope labeled with Rahu's name and place it on the table.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Tell me about your experience at the FAC.

choices.text: Tell me about your experience at the FAC.

steps.content: Rahu glances at the envelope on the table.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Why ask if you already know?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Files often contain omissions and errors. I'd like to hear your version.
Rahu doesn't waste more time and begins to talk about her past.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I was born in Syndicate, and was recruited by the FAC in N.F. 102. I'd worked for the FAC for a total of 11 years since.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Until last week. The higher-ups thought I could be of more use here.
Rahu doesn't seem too pleased when she mentions the higher-ups' decision.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Is that all? Can you go into more detail?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: What kind of detail?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: For instance, the reason you joined the FAC.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Reason?
Rahu laughs, as if it's an unwarranted, foolish question that's been asked too many times.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Ha... To survive.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Life in Syndicate is more dangerous than in the FAC.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: As far as I know, the FAC doesn't often recruit from the West District. How did you come on their radar?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: A squad was carrying out a mission in Syndicate at the time. I met their captain, who referred me to the raw recruit camp for trial training.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: And the captain's name is?
Rahu pauses for a moment, then casually says.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I don't remember.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Really?
She's lying.
The file states that after completing her training, Rahu joined that captain's squad. For almost two years, they participated in over twenty operations together.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: As far as I know, you were part of that captain's squad up until the squad was wiped out in N.F. 103.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You've repeatedly demanded the truth about the DisSea catastrophe from your superiors. You've even gone as far as barging into the FAC executives' office and making a scene. Cost you two demerits on the record.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Now, tell me again you don't remember the name of that officer?
Rahu doesn't respond and just stares intently at the file in your hand for a long time.
After a long silence, she suddenly begins.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Post-traumatic stress disorder... I've received treatment from the FAC.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: What I don't need to remember, what I shouldn't remember, I don't. This is better for me, and for everyone else.
Rahu's statements are consistent with the records in the file.
Clearly, the counter-interrogation training she received at the FAC wasn't wasted. Dwelling on this topic is pointless, and might even result in accusations of veteran persecution.
But you know she's not telling the truth, or at least not all of it. You casually flip through the file, trying to move past the previous topic.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I'm glad you were able to move on from that experience.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: ...Glad?
Rahu questions, and you can detect a barely noticeable hint of anger in her tone.
Even though she's the one who brought up things like "having received treatment" and "better for everyone," her irritation at your words still peeks through the careful concealment.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: We're not enemies here, Rahu. We're now colleagues who are about to begin a long-term working relationship.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Your eleven years at the FAC have proven your loyalty and capability. As long as you can clear up the minor flaws on your record, I would naturally be grateful to have such an excellent subordinate.
You explain. Meanwhile, you abruptly stop flipping the file, landing on the last page.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: In July N.F. 113, you left the FAC headquarters to go to Erica Villa. What for?
Taken aback by your sudden change of topic, Rahu hesitates slightly, but quickly recovers.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Vacation.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That's not a vacation spot for ordinary people.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: ...It was a private matter. I'm not answering that.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You were there to meet someone, weren't you?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You went to Erica Villa behind the back of your colleagues at the FAC, and there you met a certain big shot...

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Haha, I underestimated you...
Rahu's snicker interrupts you.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: The intelligence unit of the MBCC is quite something. What a bold move.
Rahu's smile disappears without a trace, leaving only a cold stare.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: But you better keep your subordinates in check. Don't overreach yourselves.
The threat in her words is clear, and you respond calmly.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That's none of your concern. My sources are quite reliable.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: The 9th Agency, right?
You ignore Rahu's almost provocative question and continue with the previous topic.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: What was your real purpose for going to Erica Villa?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Why don't you ask your reliable sources?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I want to hear it from you.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: They sent out a distress signal on the public channel. I received it, and then I went. It's as simple as that.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Before responding to the distress signal, did you know a high-ranking official from Paradeisos was in Erica Villa?
Rahu looks directly at you, as if she's scrutinizing you for your motive. After a few seconds of silence, she suddenly bursts into laughter.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Haha, will you take no for an answer?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Of course, I did. If the Paradeisian official wasn't there, why should I care if they were dead or alive?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: So you went for the Paradeisian official in the first place? Why?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: To butter them up so I could leave the FAC. Why else?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You'd been serving in the FAC for over ten years, why the sudden switch?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: It wasn't sudden. I'd been wanting to change jobs for a while.
Her tone no longer carries the tension of someone being interrogated, but is instead filled with casual mockery and indifference, as if she sees through you.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Indeed, I had served in the FAC for over ten years and participated in hundreds of operations, big and small. Since BR-002, my colleagues came and went. Those older and younger than me have all died, none of them had a good end.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I want to live. Those mercs working as bodyguards for Paradeisos make it to retirement alive, why can't we FAC soldiers do the same? Have we not shed enough blood already?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: A job from a Paradeisian bigwig can't be that bad.
Rahu leans back slightly and you hear the creaks of the chair.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: What about your squad? You just left them behind like that?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Not all of us are saints, ${PlayerName}. FAC soldiers are nothing more than ordinary people who feel lucky to survive another day.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Having been through so many brutal battles, it's only natural that one would want to plan ahead.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Not to mention that I don't owe them anything. I'm not irreplaceable to them either.
Rahu's voice is cold, and the facts she states are consistent with the records. Ethically speaking, she indeed had no obligation to stay in the FAC forever.
But something just doesn't sit right with you. Logically, what she says makes sense, but it doesn't exactly match her character.
These words seem like a bastion built of countless lies, so deliberately designed and seamless that it's virtually impossible to spot a crack.
Whoever this designer is, they must possess unimaginable power. Such means and power can't be found everywhere in DisCity.
The big shot from Paradeisos, the puppet master behind Rustfire, and the opportunity Rahu has mentioned. These elusive fragments are beginning to overlap in your mind.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Did that Paradeisian official accept your proposal?
Rahu seems stumped by the question, caught off guard without a well-prepared response.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Now you're here in the MBCC, not by the side of that big shot.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Have you been abandoned?
Rahu's expression gradually turns icy.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Or, is this the good job that big shot has offered you? Transferring to the MBCC?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Let's see... You're an experienced and powerful combatant, an elite who can be entrusted with important tasks anywhere.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Why give up such a capable assistant and send you to me?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: To kill me? No, too inefficient. To watch me? Possibly.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: But why would that big shot ignore the 9th Agency and directly monitor me instead? Is it about Rustfire? Or maybe it's related to the attack I suffered at the Drifter Camp...

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Hahaha...
The cold, abrupt snicker interrupts you.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I've seen many like you who thought they could see through everything and grasp the truth.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Guess what happened to them?
Rahu's smile is overlaid with a shadow.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Are you threatening me?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Consider this a threat if you will.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Your curiosity is too brazen, whether it's about the truth or that big shot... Your thoughts are practically written all over your face.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: Stop deluding yourself that you can pursue the truth. Know your place, you're only the chief of this little bureau. Or else, you risk your life.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: You've been doing well so far. Stop now, and they might overlook this little misbehavior.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: But if you insist on pushing further, well...
Rahu looks up, her eyes flashing with a dangerous light.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: DisCity is built on the bones of those who betray and cross the line. No one can protect you, not even the 9th Agency.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: You're dealing with that kind of big shot.
Rahu's tone is incredibly calm, but what's hidden beneath the calm surface makes your hair stand on end for a moment.
You take a deep breath, trying to calm yourself.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Thank you for your advice, Rahu.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I think I can tame my curiosity. I can get the information I need without crossing the line.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: At least I won't end up like Conrad Cage.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: ...Conrad?
You catch a complex emotion flickering in Rahu's eyes at the mention of this name.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Don't you know?

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I'm not sure what you mean by that.
Her face no longer changes, all emotions hidden behind those cold eyes.

Conrad Cage joined the FAC in N.F. 100. He was in the G47 squad just like you. In N.F. 103, he missed the DisSea operation due to injury. He and you ended up being the only two survivors of the G47 squad that year.
After that, he took over the position of the previous officer, becoming your direct superior. For over a decade, you served in the same squad.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Until █ months ago, shortly after you went to Erica Villa, Conrad's squad suffered an accident in a battle...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: In short, he was the only survivor in the whole squad.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Or rather, you two are. After all, you're still officially part of the G47 squad.
Rahu's pupils suddenly contract. What baffles you is that she seems to be in complete disbelief after hearing these facts from you.
As if she just heard it for the first time.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Rings a bell, doesn't it?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Ten years ago, you belonged to the same squad. He was absent due to injury, and you were the only survivor of the battle.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I thought you two had a good relationship. After all, he was your direct superior, and also the one who vouched for you when you left the squad to go to Erica Villa...

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: What happened to him?
Rahu interrupts you.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...A lot.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: According to the FAC, Conrad has been affected by Mania and is facing serious mental issues.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: He blames everything in DisCity on conspiracy and that he's seen... Well, in short, he's been spreading some anti-social rhetoric.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Not only that, he planned an attack against some important person and seriously jeopardized public safety. Fortunately, the plan was exposed before it could cause major damage.

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: And what does this have to do with me?
Unconsciously, Rahu's expression changes from suspicious to cautious.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Relax, you're not under suspicion yet. However...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: However, Conrad's treatment isn't going well. He's undergone rigorous psychological training in the past, which is now working against him. He specifically refuses treatment from doctors and has even shown highly aggressive behaviors.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: A professional institution has contacted the FAC, claiming they can take over him and provide him with appropriate treatment. However, the FAC hasn't accepted the offer yet.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: They're seeking help from us, an organization experienced in dealing with those infected with Mania... Perhaps because they know that you've recently been transferred here.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: You see, the MBCC has always been an open book to other departments.
Nino

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: They probably don't expect much from me. Instead, I think they're hoping that you, Conrad's former comrade, can provide some help.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Of course, I completely understand if you don't want to go. All I can do is try to get Conrad's version of the truth. Hopefully that'll at least help the FAC's medical department analyze the cause of his mental disorder...

steps.speaker: Rahu
steps.content: I'll go.
Rahu's answer is curt but firm.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Great.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: This is your first field assignment in the Bureau. Break a leg.
Rahu doesn't respond to that. Somehow, the two of you seem to have reached a mutual understanding.
Rather than to help a former comrade, she's probably agreed to go in order to monitor any potential meddling on your part. But that doesn't matter.
You've achieved your goal.
